questions.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?

options.explanation: Newton is the SI unit of force, not pressure.
Joule is the SI unit of energy, not pressure.
Pascal is the correct SI unit of pressure.
Watt is the SI unit of power, not pressure.

questions.explanation: The SI unit of pressure is Pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to Newton per square meter (N/m²).
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: Which type of friction is generally the least among static, sliding, rolling, and fluid friction?

options.explanation: Static friction is the highest type of friction as it prevents the start of motion.
Sliding friction is less than static friction but more than rolling friction.
Rolling friction is the least among the given options.
Fluid friction depends on the viscosity of the fluid and can vary but is generally not the least in all contexts.

questions.explanation: Rolling friction is always less than sliding friction, and sliding friction is less than static friction. This is why it is easier to roll objects than to slide them.
questions.hint: Think about the ease of movement when rolling versus sliding an object.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: Why are school bags provided with wide straps?

options.text: It makes the bag look stylish.
options.explanation: The primary purpose of wide straps is functional, not aesthetic.

options.text: It distributes the weight over a smaller area.
options.explanation: Distributing weight over a smaller area increases pressure, which is not desirable.

options.text: It distributes the weight over a larger area, reducing the pressure on the shoulders.
options.explanation: Wide straps reduce pressure by increasing the area over which the weight is distributed.

options.text: It increases the force exerted by the bag.
options.explanation: The force exerted by the bag is its weight, which cannot be increased by changing the strap width.

questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as Force/Area. By increasing the area (wide straps), the pressure exerted on the shoulders by the same force (weight of the bag) is reduced, making it more comfortable to carry.
questions.hint: Consider how pressure changes with area when the force remains constant.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a possible effect of force acting on an object?

options.text: Change in the state of motion
options.explanation: Force can change the state of motion of an object.

options.text: Change in the shape of the object
options.explanation: Force can deform an object, changing its shape.

options.text: Change in the direction of motion
options.explanation: Force can alter the direction in which an object moves.

options.text: Change in the mass of the object
options.explanation: Force cannot change the mass of an object; mass is an intrinsic property.

questions.explanation: Force can change the speed, direction, or state of motion (from rest to motion or vice-versa) of an object, and it can also change its shape. However, force does not change the mass of an object.
questions.hint: Remember the basic effects of force: motion, direction, shape, but not mass.

questions.question: Calculate the pressure exerted when a force of 500 N is applied on an area of 0.5 m².

options.explanation: 100 Pa is incorrect as the calculation yields a different value.
250 Pa is incorrect; the correct calculation is 1000 Pa.
500 Pa is incorrect; the correct calculation is 1000 Pa.
1000 Pa is the correct pressure calculated from the given values.

questions.explanation: Pressure is calculated as Force divided by Area. Here, P = 500 N / 0.5 m² = 1000 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula Pressure = Force / Area.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: A suction cup sticks to a smooth, flat surface primarily due to:

options.text: Adhesive forces between the cup and the surface.
options.explanation: While adhesives can help, the primary force here is atmospheric pressure.

options.text: The weight of the suction cup.
options.explanation: The weight of the cup is negligible compared to atmospheric pressure.

options.text: Atmospheric pressure pushing on the outside of the cup.
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the primary reason the suction cup sticks.
Suction cups do not rely on magnetic forces to stick.

questions.explanation: When a suction cup is pressed against a smooth surface, the air inside is pushed out, creating a region of lower pressure inside the cup. The higher atmospheric pressure acting on the outside of the cup then pushes it firmly against the surface.
questions.hint: Think about the role of air pressure in making the suction cup stick.

questions.question: Which method would effectively decrease friction between two surfaces?

options.explanation: Rough surfaces increase friction due to interlocking irregularities.

options.text: Applying a lubricant like oil or grease.
options.explanation: Lubricants reduce friction by forming a slippery layer between surfaces.

options.text: Increasing the normal force pressing the surfaces together.
options.explanation: Increasing normal force generally increases friction.

options.text: Increasing the area of contact between the surfaces.
options.explanation: Increasing area does not significantly reduce friction.

questions.explanation: Lubricants like oil or grease form a thin layer between surfaces, reducing direct contact and thus friction. Making surfaces rougher or increasing the normal force would increase friction.
questions.hint: Lubricants reduce friction by separating surfaces.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is easier to move a loaded trolley with wheels than to drag it on the ground. Reason (R): Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are correct, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains why the assertion is true.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason is also true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because wheels reduce friction (rolling friction). The reason is also true, as rolling friction is indeed smaller than sliding friction, and the reason directly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Compare rolling friction and sliding friction to understand the assertion and reason.

questions.question: A wooden block measures 10 cm x 5 cm x 2 cm. If its mass is 200 g, what is the maximum pressure it can exert on a surface? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

options.explanation: 2000 Pa is incorrect; the correct pressure is much higher.
4000 Pa is incorrect; the correct pressure is 20000 Pa.
20000 Pa is the correct maximum pressure calculated from the given values.
40000 Pa is incorrect; the correct pressure is 20000 Pa.

questions.explanation: To exert maximum pressure, the block must be placed on its smallest area. The smallest area is 5 cm x 2 cm = 10 cm² = 0.001 m². Force = mass × gravity = 0.2 kg × 10 m/s² = 2 N. Pressure = Force / Area = 2 N / 0.001 m² = 20000 Pa.
questions.hint: Calculate pressure using the smallest possible area of contact.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about friction is INCORRECT?

options.text: Friction always opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about friction.

options.text: Friction can be a necessary evil in many daily activities.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about friction.

options.text: Lubricants are used to increase friction between moving parts.
options.explanation: Lubricants reduce friction, making this statement incorrect.

options.text: Static friction is generally greater than kinetic (sliding) friction.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about friction.

questions.explanation: Lubricants are used to reduce friction, not increase it. The other statements are correct descriptions of friction.
questions.hint: Identify the statement that contradicts the properties of friction and lubricants.

questions.question: A push or a pull acting on an object is commonly referred to as a:

options.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, not the action itself.
Energy is the capacity to do work, not the action of pushing or pulling.
Correct. Force is a push or pull.
Work is done when a force moves an object over a distance.

questions.explanation: Force is defined as a push or a pull that can change the state of motion or shape of an object.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: The SI unit of pressure is:

options.explanation: Newton is the SI unit of force, not pressure.
Joule is the SI unit of energy or work, not pressure.
Correct. Pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure.
Watt is the SI unit of power, not pressure.

questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as force per unit area. The SI unit of force is Newton (N) and area is square meter (m²), so the unit of pressure is N/m², which is also called Pascal (Pa).
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: If a constant force is applied over a larger area, the pressure exerted will:

options.explanation: Pressure decreases when the area increases with constant force.
Correct. Pressure decreases as area increases.
Pressure changes when the area changes.
Pressure changes uniformly with area, not in stages.

questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area over which the force acts (P = F/A). If the area increases while the force remains constant, the pressure decreases.
questions.hint: Recall the formula for pressure: P = F/A.

questions.question: Which of the following types of friction is generally the smallest?

options.explanation: Static friction is the friction that prevents an object from starting to move.
Sliding friction acts when an object slides over a surface.
Correct. Rolling friction is the smallest.
Kinetic friction is another term for sliding friction.

questions.explanation: Rolling friction is generally much smaller than static friction and sliding (kinetic) friction because the contact area between the surfaces is very small and the object is rolling rather than sliding, reducing the interlocking of irregularities.
questions.hint: Consider the nature of motion in each type of friction.

questions.question: A force of 300 N is applied uniformly over an area of 5 m². Calculate the pressure exerted.

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation. 300 N / 5 m² = 60 Pa, not 1500 Pa.
Correct. The pressure is 60 Pa.
Incorrect. The correct calculation yields 60 Pa.
Incorrect. The correct calculation yields 60 Pa.

questions.explanation: Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A). Given F = 300 N, A = 5 m². P = 300 N / 5 m² = 60 N/m² = 60 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula P = F/A.

questions.question: A suction cup sticks to a smooth, flat surface primarily due to:

options.explanation: Magnetic force is not involved in a suction cup sticking.
Gravitational force acts downward and does not cause the suction cup to stick.
Correct. Atmospheric pressure pushes the suction cup against the surface.
Muscular force is used to press the cup, but the sticking is due to atmospheric pressure.

questions.explanation: When a suction cup is pressed against a surface, air inside is pushed out, creating a partial vacuum. The higher atmospheric pressure outside the cup then pushes it firmly against the surface.
questions.hint: Consider the role of air pressure in this scenario.

questions.question: Which of the following actions would *increase* the friction between two surfaces in contact?

options.explanation: Polishing reduces the roughness of the surfaces, decreasing friction.
Lubricants reduce friction by creating a slippery layer between surfaces.
Correct. Rougher surfaces increase friction due to more interlocking.

options.text: Reducing the normal force pressing the surfaces together
options.explanation: Reducing the normal force decreases friction.

questions.explanation: Friction is caused by the interlocking of irregularities on the surfaces in contact. Making the surfaces rougher increases these irregularities, leading to greater interlocking and thus increased friction. Polishing, applying lubricants, and reducing the normal force all decrease friction.
questions.hint: Think about what factors increase friction.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: Arrange the following types of friction in increasing order of their magnitude: (i) Static friction (ii) Sliding friction (iii) Rolling friction

options.explanation: Incorrect order. The correct order is (iii), (ii), (i).
Correct. Rolling friction < Sliding friction < Static friction.
Incorrect order.
Incorrect order.

questions.explanation: Rolling friction is the smallest, followed by sliding (kinetic) friction, and static friction is the largest. It takes the most force to initiate motion (overcome static friction), less to keep an object sliding (kinetic friction), and even less to keep an object rolling.
questions.hint: Consider the ease of starting and maintaining motion for each type.

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** It is generally easier to pull a heavy suitcase fitted with wheels than to push it. **Reason (R):** When pushing, the downward component of the applied force increases the normal force and thus friction, while when pulling, the upward component of the applied force reduces the normal force and thus friction.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason is also true.

questions.explanation: When pushing an object, if the force is applied downwards at an angle, its vertical component adds to the object's weight, increasing the normal force and consequently the friction. Conversely, when pulling upwards at an angle, the vertical component of the force reduces the effective weight, decreasing the normal force and friction, making it easier to move.
questions.hint: Analyze how the direction of the applied force affects the normal force.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: A deep-sea diver experiences immense pressure at great depths. This pressure primarily increases due to:

options.text: The density of seawater increasing significantly with depth.
options.explanation: While density increases slightly with depth, it is not the primary reason for the immense pressure increase.

options.text: The decrease in atmospheric pressure acting on the water surface.
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, but this does not cause the pressure to increase with depth in water.

options.text: The increasing weight of the column of water above the diver.
options.explanation: Correct. The pressure increases due to the weight of the water column above the diver.

options.text: The temperature of the water decreasing significantly at greater depths.
options.explanation: Temperature changes do not significantly affect the pressure at depth.

questions.explanation: Pressure in a fluid (P) is directly proportional to the depth (h), density of the fluid (ρ), and acceleration due to gravity (g), given by P = hρg. As the depth (h) increases, the height and thus the weight of the water column above the diver increases, leading to a proportional increase in pressure. Changes in water density or temperature are not the primary reasons for this significant pressure increase, and atmospheric pressure acts on the surface but doesn't directly explain the increase with depth.
questions.hint: Recall the formula for pressure in a fluid: P = hρg.
questions.subject: maha8-physics

questions.question: What type of friction comes into play when an object is at rest on a surface and an external force is applied but is not strong enough to move it?

options.explanation: Sliding friction occurs when an object slides over a surface.
Static friction is the correct type as it acts when the object is at rest and the applied force is insufficient to move it.
Rolling friction occurs when an object rolls over a surface.
Fluid friction occurs when an object moves through a fluid like air or water.

questions.explanation: Static friction is the force that opposes the initiation of motion when an object is at rest on a surface. It acts to prevent the object from moving until the applied force exceeds a certain maximum value.
questions.hint: This friction acts when an object is stationary despite an applied force.

questions.question: A sharp knife cuts vegetables more easily than a blunt knife. This is because:

options.text: The sharp knife has more force.
options.explanation: The force applied by both knives is the same; the difference lies in the contact area.

options.text: The blunt knife creates more friction.
options.explanation: While friction is involved, it is not the primary reason for the sharp knife cutting more easily.

options.text: The sharp knife has a smaller contact area, thus exerting more pressure for the same force.
options.explanation: This is the correct explanation as pressure increases with a decrease in contact area for the same force.
The weight of the knife does not directly affect its cutting ability in this context.

questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as Force/Area. A sharp knife has a very small cutting edge (area). When the same amount of force is applied, the smaller area results in significantly higher pressure, which helps in cutting through the vegetable more easily.
questions.hint: Consider the relationship between the area of contact and the pressure exerted.

questions.question: A block of wood weighing 50 N rests on a table. If the area of contact between the block and the table is 0.2 m², what is the pressure exerted by the block on the table?

options.explanation: This value is incorrect. The correct calculation yields a higher value.
This value is incorrect. The correct calculation yields a higher value.
This value is incorrect. The correct calculation yields a higher value.
The correct calculation of pressure is 50 N / 0.2 m² = 250 Pa.

questions.explanation: Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A). Given Force (F) = 50 N and Area (A) = 0.2 m², P = 50 / 0.2 = 250 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula Pressure = Force / Area.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Athletes use shoes with spikes to get a better grip while running. Reason (R): Spikes increase the contact area with the ground, thereby reducing friction.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: While A is true, R is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: A is true, and R is false as spikes reduce contact area and increase friction.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true, so this option is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true. Spikes on athletic shoes improve grip. However, Reason (R) is false. Spikes decrease the contact area and dig into the ground, increasing friction by interlocking, which prevents slipping.
questions.hint: Evaluate the truth of both the assertion and the reason, and whether the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.question: A child is playing with three different toys: a toy car with wheels, a wooden block, and a toy boat floating in water. If the child wants to move these toys across a dry floor, which toy will require the least force to keep it in motion, and why?

options.text: The wooden block, because it has a large surface area for contact.
options.explanation: A larger surface area does not necessarily mean less friction; sliding friction is generally higher than rolling friction.

options.text: The toy boat, because water provides lubrication.
options.explanation: The toy boat is on a dry floor, so water lubrication is irrelevant here.

options.text: The toy car, because rolling friction is generally less than sliding friction.
options.explanation: Rolling friction is less than sliding friction, so the toy car requires the least force to keep in motion.

options.text: All three will require the same force as friction depends only on the weight.
options.explanation: Friction depends on the type of contact (e.g., rolling vs. sliding) and not solely on weight.

questions.explanation: The toy car has wheels, which means it experiences rolling friction when moved. The wooden block and toy boat experience sliding friction. Rolling friction is significantly less than sliding friction.
questions.hint: Consider the types of friction each toy will experience when moved across a dry floor.
